subject: Mapping cloud SOC evidence to Redwood subservice responsibilities — evidence & bridge letter request
messages:
From: Lydia Park <security@fintechlabs.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: SOC 2 Type II + subservice evidence mapping

Hi Stephanie,

We're starting our vendor assurance for FinTech Labs' upcoming audit and need to collect SOC 2 Type II evidence for the period Jan 1 2026 - Dec 31 2026. Specifically:

- A copy of Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report covering the period above (or a bridge letter if your audit window doesn't align).
- A mapping that shows which controls are covered by Redwood vs which you rely on cloud providers (GCP/AWS) or subprocessors.
- A roster of subprocessors (name, service, data access scope).
- Any bridge-letter language you can provide that references provider SOC reports (e.g., GCP) and clarifies carve-outs / shared responsibility.

I've attached our SOC evidence request form (SOC-request-form.xlsx) with fields we prefer you populate. Can you confirm what you can provide and an ETA? We're targeting to close vendor evidence collection by 2027-05-14.

Thanks,
Lydia Park
Security Lead, FinTech Labs
security@fintechlabs.com

Attachments: SOC-request-form.xlsx

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-05T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SOC 2 Type II + subservice evidence mapping

Hi Lydia,

Thanks for the clear ask — we can support this. High-level response and plan: 

1) We'll provide our SOC 2 Type II report for the closest audit period (attached as redwood_soc2_typeii_2026.pdf). If the audit window isn't a perfect match for your Jan–Dec 2026 window, we'll include a bridge letter that calls out the provider reports we rely on and the overlapping dates.

2) Attached is a draft provider-control-mapping workbook (provider-mapping-draft.xlsx) that separates controls we operate from controls we rely on (GCP). Please review and tell us if you want it formatted by SOC category (CCM) or by technical control.

3) We'll also share our current subprocessor roster (subprocessor_roster.csv) and a bridge-letter template that we can tailor to reference GCP's SOC report(s).

I'll ask Aditya (security infra) to add the technical notes on KMS/keys and data isolation, and Jasmine to confirm timing and any procurement-level paperwork. Can we aim to get the populated mapping and bridge letter draft to you by 2027-05-07 EOD?

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Security & Compliance (acting)
Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_soc2_typeii_2026.pdf, provider-mapping-draft.xlsx, subprocessor_roster.csv, bridge-letter-template.docx

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Park <security@fintechlabs.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-05T11:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SOC 2 Type II + subservice evidence mapping

Hi Lydia / team,

Quick technical clarifications to help populate the mapping workbook: 

- Infrastructure (physical security, datacenter controls, host maintenance) — we rely on GCP's SOC 2 reports. We can reference the exact GCP report IDs in the mapping.
- Compute & runtime (container orchestration, application layer) — managed and operated by Redwood; control evidence available (config snapshots, deploy logs).
- Storage & backups — primary storage is GCS; encryption at rest is provided by GCP KMS. We maintain application-level envelope encryption for customer secrets; key usage logs can be produced (redacted).
- Networking — VPC configuration and egress controls are within our responsibility; cloud network segmentation is a shared responsibility (we'll provide VPC config exports).
- Access management — Redwood IAM + SSO; we can provide role rosters and recent access reviews.

Regarding the bridge letter: our proposed language will explicitly reference the GCP SOC 2 report(s) we rely on and state the scope of reliance (e.g., physical and host controls). We do not intend to carve out logical controls that Redwood operates.

If you need KMS usage logs, tell us the level of detail (per-key activity vs aggregate) and we'll scope that in the delivery.

– Aditya
Security Infrastructure
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

From: Lydia Park <security@fintechlabs.com>

Stephanie / Aditya,

Thanks — that level of detail helps. A few follow-ups: 

- The audit team has asked that any bridge letter explicitly name the provider SOC report(s) (GCP SOC 2 Type II) and include the provider report period so we can confirm overlap.
- For KMS evidence, we require per-key usage logs for the primary keys that protect customer secrets for the 2026 audit year (redacted principal IDs are fine). Please confirm you can supply that or a summary table.
- For subprocessors, please include a column for "data access scope" (e.g., logs-only, stored data, full access) — that's critical for our risk assessment.

Can you confirm an updated due date? If you can get the mapping and KMS scope to us by 2027-05-07, that would be ideal; otherwise we'll need an explicit delivery date so procurement can schedule the review.

Best,
Lydia
Security Lead, FinTech Labs
